_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#0, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: scikit-fem has NO built-in Newton solver or NS assembly, so both must be hand-coded; signal is that searching skfem.utils for NewtonSolver or NavierStokes returns no match. Ran: 15 plausible names for a nonlinear solver, an NS assembly and a time integrator probed against both the skfem and skfem.utils namespaces, the full 47-name public surface of skfem.utils enumerated, and the building blocks a hand-rolled Newton needs checked for presence. Printed: none of the 15 names exists in either namespace. The positive half is the useful part -- skfem.utils exposes LINEAR and EIGEN solvers only (solve, solve_linear, solve_eigen, the solver_iter_* family, condense/enforce/penalize) and nothing that iterates on a nonlinear residual, so the absence is structural rather than a naming accident. All six building blocks (BilinearForm, LinearForm, Basis, asm, condense, solve) ARE present, which is why the catalog ships snippets rather than a call. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): this fixture asserts an ABSENCE, so the control injects the thing the claim says is missing rather than removing a pathology -- T2_MUTATE=1 binds skfem.utils.NewtonSolver before the probe runs. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 5 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'nonlinear_names_found=[]', 'no_nonlinear_solver_anywhere=True' and 'utils_offers_only_linear_and_eigen_solvers=True' so the fixture goes red, which proves those lines are read off the namespace rather than hard-coded. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
